text:
alex: heads-up - onboarding sample upload flow is flaky on some Android devices. large file uploads (20-100MB) sometimes fail with truncated data after a token refresh, looks like request body was consumed and replay attempted.

renee: ugh. streaming bodies + retries = classic. which retrofit/okhttp? exact failure logs?

alex: Retrofit 2.9.0, OkHttp 4.9.3 (packaged in our SDK). repro on Android 9 emulator and a couple of Pixel devices. logs: 

W/OkHttp: java.io.IOException: unexpected end of stream on Connection{10.0.2.2:8080, proxy=DIRECT} (recycle count 0)
E/UploadWorker: java.io.IOException: request body was already consumed, cannot retry

jay: are you using an Interceptor to refresh tokens? or Authenticator?

alex: interceptor atm. simplified snippet in the sample:```kotlin
class StreamingRequestBody(private val input: InputStream): RequestBody() {
  override fun contentType() = "application/octet-stream".toMediaTypeOrNull()
  override fun writeTo(sink: BufferedSink) {
    input.source().use { src -> sink.writeAll(src) }
  }
}
// retrofit call uses MultipartBody.Part.createFormData(..., StreamingRequestBody(stream))
```

pradeep: yep that won't be repeatable. if the client needs to retry (auth refresh or network), OkHttp cannot re-run the body. Interceptor-based refresh that does chain.proceed() again will try to re-send the same streaming body and fail.

renee: two paths: 1) make the body repeatable (buffer to disk or memory) so retries work, 2) avoid re-sending by doing auth at the connection layer using an Authenticator + separate client for token fetching, or 3) ensure uploads are single-shot and do resumable uploads server-side (preferred long term).

jay: for the sample app we should show a minimal change: wrap large uploads in a TempFileRequestBody that writes the stream to a temp file and then uses that file for RequestBody so retry/clone works. add cleanup afterwards. fast to implement and explains trade-offs.

alex: tried a simple buffer-to-memory for 50MB and OOM'd on low-end devices. temp file approach worked on Pixel 3 emulator. code-skel:```kotlin
class FileBackedRequestBody(private val tmp: File, private val contentType: MediaType?): RequestBody() {
  override fun contentType() = contentType
  override fun contentLength() = tmp.length()
  override fun writeTo(sink: BufferedSink) {
    tmp.source().use { sink.writeAll(it) }
  }
}
```

pradeep: also consider header hints: if you can set Content-Length (fixed length) OkHttp may avoid chunked streaming which interacts better with some proxies. But that doesn't solve the source being consumed.

renee: add a paragraph in the sample README: "When uploading large files from Android clients, prefer resumable uploads or a file-backed request body. Streaming request bodies are not repeatable and will be lost on retry."

alex: i pushed a sample change with FileBackedRequestBody + cleanup task and a tiny instrumentation test emulating concurrent 401 during upload: 1935674345-alex-filebacked-upload-fix PR.

infra-bot: CI started for branch alex/file-upload-fix (build #2087) :gear:

jay: small SDK note: we should document "RequestBody repeatability" in our Java/Kotlin SDK docs. show examples: in-memory (small files), disk-backed (large), and resumable server pattern. link to sample PR.

pradeep: bonus tip: if you control server, support a HEAD-based resumable handshake so client can resume offset after refresh rather than replaying whole body. much friendlier for mobile.

renee: also add a short devex blurb: "Auth interceptor vs Authenticator: Interceptor runs at application layer and can cause body replay issues for streaming bodies; Authenticator is invoked by OkHttp on 401 and better preserves connection semantics — but use a dedicated client for token calls to avoid recursive auth loops."

alex: confirmed FileBackedRequestBody fixed truncated uploads on Pixel 3 emulator and a Pixel 6 physical device. CI tests passed locally.

infra-bot: CI build #2087 passed :white_check_mark:

alex: merging and will backport to sample release v0.11. Also filing SDK docs ticket: DEX-412 (document repeatable bodies + auth patterns).

jay: thanks! can someone add a small e2e that injects a 401 mid-upload in the test server so we catch regressions?

pradeep: I'll add a flaky guard and a deterministic server-side toggle for tests.

renee: great discussion. Alex — include an explicit repro section in PR description (emulator ADB commands, logcat snippet, path to failing test) so oncall can triage customer reports faster.

alex: will do. thanks all :thumbsup:
